final_answer:
MEMORANDUM (Privileged). To: C. Archer, GC. From: Whitmore & Kessler. Re: Pinnacle 2025 DEF 14A (draft v7.2) compliance gap analysis.

BOTTOM LINE
Do not file April 28 as drafted. Five critical defects create Rule 14a-9 and Say-on-Pay exposure, particularly with Leland Cross: (1) SCT/CD&A annual incentive figures contradict the Committee minutes; (2) the 140% payout factor is arithmetically unsupported; (3) Chen's spouse-affiliated $380,000 Broadleaf transaction is omitted; (4) Proposal 5 eligibility and procedure are doubtful; (5) Pay Versus Performance (PvP) is incomplete. The in-house checklist is wrong in many places (Part C). Basis: the six supplied documents only; only the Chen and Frederickson questionnaires were supplied, and the form of proxy, 13D/Gs and 10-K were not. SEC/eCFR sites were unreachable, so rule citations are from knowledge and must be cite-checked.

A. TIER 1 - CRITICAL

1. Annual incentive: SCT vs. minutes (Item 402(c)(2)(vii), (d)).
- Minutes (Feb. 20, 2025, Sec. V) approved payouts: Villanueva $1,813,000; Langford $875,000; Poole $724,500; Isaacs $705,600; Archer $642,600. The draft SCT reports target amounts ($1,295,000/$687,500/$603,750/$588,000/$513,000). Your email says payouts were "confirmed at target"; that contradicts the CD&A's 140% and Item 402(c), which requires amounts earned.
- Target percentages conflict: draft Langford 110%, Poole 105%, Isaacs 105%, Archer 95%; minutes 100%, 90%, 90%, 85% (targets $625,000/$517,500/$504,000/$459,000). Villanueva matches. The CD&A target table and Grants of Plan-Based Awards (GPBA) threshold/target/maximum are affected.
- If the minutes control, FY2024 SCT totals become: Villanueva $6,387,800 (not $5,869,800); Langford $3,137,000; Poole $2,616,000; Isaacs $2,485,100; Archer $2,184,100 (before item 6). This flows into the Proxy Summary, pay ratio (about 94.7:1 on $67,469, not 87:1), PvP and severance tables.
- Action: confirm targets and payouts with the plan document, payroll and Committee before filing.

2. The 140% factor does not follow from the plan formula (Item 402(b)(2)(v)-(vii); Rule 14a-9).
- Minutes' individual factors (155%/170%/57.5%) do not match their own scales: EBITDA ($590M target/$708M max) gives 118.6%; revenue growth (7.0%/10.5%) gives 134.3%; FCF ($240M-$300M) gives 87.5%, not 57.5%. Blended is about 117.1%.
- The draft CD&A uses different goal schedules (EBITDA $530M/$590M/$680M; revenue 4.0%/7.0%/12.0%; FCF max $370M) than the minutes ($531M/$590M/$708M; 3.5%/7.0%/10.5%; $360M). On the draft's scales blended is about 116.9%.
- Either way the formula yields roughly 117%. The CD&A says no discretion was used, so it would be false. CEO excess is roughly $297,000 ($1,813,000 vs. about $1,516,000), proportionally for others. Rothwell's "verification" and CD&A sign-off cannot be relied on.
- Action: obtain the plan's goals and re-run; Committee to re-certify, or if it intends 140%, disclose positive discretion and rationale; address any payments made; disclose goals and per-metric payouts (your checklist C-06 is already "Partial"). Clawback (Item 402(w)) is not triggered absent a restatement.

3. Chen/Broadleaf omitted (Items 404(a), 407(a)(3), 404(b)).
- Chen's questionnaire: $380,000 paid in FY2024 to Broadleaf Consulting, in which her spouse holds about 20% as equity partner. Over $120,000, spouse is an immediate family member: Item 404(a) disclosure is required (relationship, interest, amount, value of related person's interest). The draft lists only Goss and the Harmon lease; checklist R-04 ("none additional") is wrong.
- Item 407(a)(3) requires describing relationships considered in independence determinations; the draft says no independent director has any material relationship. NYSE 303A.02(b) bright-line tests are probably not triggered, but Chen's cited "$1 million/2%" test applies to family members who are executive officers of the payee; confirm Gerald Chen's status. The Board must still document an affirmative determination for the Lead Independent Director.
- Approval conflict: Chen says the N&G Committee approved (March 14, 2024) with her recused; the draft says the Audit Committee administers the RPT Policy (checklist R-01 says N&G). N&G has two members including Chen. Determine the approving body and disclose accurately.
- Harmon lease: add amounts paid in FY2024 ($216,000), aggregate remaining payments ($684,000) and Harmon's interest.

4. Proposal 5 - Leland Cross (Rule 14a-8).
- Eligibility: Leland Cross acquired its 6.8% in Q4 2024 and submitted January 15, 2025, yet you state verified one-year continuous ownership of $25,000. Rule 14a-8(b)(1)(i) requires one year at submission; a Q4 2024 purchase cannot satisfy that absent earlier holdings. Obtain the broker proof letter and 13D/G history.
- Procedure: Rule 14a-8(f)(1) required a deficiency notice within 14 days of receipt and 14a-8(j) a no-action request 80 days before filing (about February 7). If neither occurred, exclusion is likely waived/unavailable; do not describe the proponent as eligible in any document until verified, and consider litigation counsel.
- Rule 14a-8(m)(3): the opposition statement should have gone to the proponent at least 30 days before filing (about March 29). Confirm.
- Length: proposal and supporting statement are about 300 words, within the 500-word limit (14a-8(d)); proponent name, address and share count are included (14a-8(l)). No cap applies to the Company's statement.
- Opposition statement risks (Rule 14a-9): it touts Harmon's value "during the CEO transition" though the transition occurred January 1, 2024, and omits Harmon's related-party lease and son-in-law's employment, which bear on his independence. Consider balancing disclosure. Verify the "majority of votes cast" standard against the charter/bylaws.

5. Pay Versus Performance (Item 402(v)).
- The table covers three years (FY2022-2024). A non-smaller-reporting company filing in 2025 must cover five (FY2020-2024); the checklist (C-23, E-04) and email repeat the error.
- PEO misidentified: Villanueva is shown as 2023 PEO, but Harmon was CEO through December 31, 2023. Name each PEO per year and show both if both served.
- Non-PEO 2023 average ($2,263,194) does not equal the average of the draft's SCT figures ($2,263,244). CAP footnote lacks the amount-by-amount adjustments (Item 402(v)(3)). All SCT-driven numbers change with item 1. Tabular measures list (five unranked) is acceptable.

B. TIER 2 - IMPORTANT

6. SCT presentation (Item 402(c)). Only two years shown; three required for persons who were NEOs earlier (checklist C-15 says three). Footnote 3 reports 401(k) match "earnings" for Archer in the pension/NQDC column, which is improper (only above-market NQDC earnings qualify; match is already in All Other). Perquisites over $10,000 must be quantified and identified; Villanueva's car allowance is $28,000 (checklist C-09 says none exceeds $25,000). Titles differ from minutes (Poole "EVP & COO," Isaacs "SVP, Strategy," Archer "SVP"); confirm NEO roles.

7. CD&A (Item 402(b)). Peer companies not named (checklist says 16, minutes say 20). Item 402(x) option-grant timing policy disclosure absent. Director RSU vesting differs from minutes (earlier of one year or next annual meeting).

8. Comp Committee interlocks (Item 407(e)(4)). Omitted; checklist D-11 marks "N/A" but a negative statement is required. Frederickson's questionnaire says Isaacs (Pinnacle EVP) sits on Clearway's board with her. Obtain Isaacs' questionnaire and Clearway committee roles; confirm no Clearway executive serves on Pinnacle's Board or Compensation Committee, and assess independence.

9. Frederickson bio vs. questionnaire (Item 401(e)). Proxy: Dalton Capital Senior Advisor since 2018; Clearway CHRO 2005-2017; Duke MBA; Clearway director since 2018. Questionnaire: no employer; Meridian Technologies SVP Strategy 2005-2017; Carlisle MBA; Clearway director since March 2017; options under a "2019 Equity Incentive Plan" (draft names only 2020 and 2012 plans). Resolve against primary sources. She sits on four public boards including Pinnacle; checklist D-15 "none above 3" is arguable; review overboarding policy.

10. Insider trading/hedging (Items 407(i), 408(b)). Draft says the hedging ban covers directors and executive officers; the policy (Sec. VI) covers all employees, directors and officers (and family and controlled entities). Item 407(i) requires accurate coverage description. Policy is silent on pledging and the Company's own trading; Item 408(b)(1) requires stating whether Company-level policies exist. Item 408(b)(2) requires the policy as an exhibit (10-K). Checklist E-07 says disclosure is in the CD&A; it is not. Item 408(a) 10b5-1 disclosure belongs in 10-Q/10-K, so E-08's proxy reference is misplaced.

11. Beneficial ownership (Item 403). Harmon: Summary and bio say 1,620,000 (1.96%); table says 1,740,000 (2.11%, with options); reconcile. The email names the 9.00% holder "Vanguard Capital Management"; draft and checklist say "Saxonbrook Capital Management" - verify against the 13G. Sole/shared voting and dispositive power for 5% holders missing. Table date March 15 vs. record date April 14: confirm shares outstanding. Frederickson's footnote says family limited partnership with spouse; her questionnaire says a trust with sole dispositive power. Confirm group count (all executive officers).

12. Equity plan table (Item 201(d)). Column (a) 2,100,000 vs. footnote components totaling 2,185,000. Checklist says the 2012 Plan is not shareholder-approved; the draft places it in "approved." The $42.15 WAEP cannot be reconciled with the checklist's 2012 plan WAEP of $28.50. Checklist E-03 is "Partial".

13. Section 16 (Item 405). Poole's grant was Friday March 15, 2024; Form 4 due March 19; filed March 22 is three business days late, not two. The 18,000-RSU grant conflicts with the GPBA (12,396 PSUs; 8,264 RSUs). No materiality qualifier exists; the "minor" characterization should not appear. Check other filers.

14. Virtual meeting. Draft lacks technical-support contact, question/conduct rules, shareholder-list access, beneficial-holder participation procedures (staff guidance; DGCL 211, 219). Verify charter/bylaws permit virtual-only. Checklist G-12 "Complete" overstated.

15. Delivery model. Checklist says notice-and-access (Rule 14a-16: notice at least 40 days before meeting, by May 3); the draft says the full package is being mailed. Choose one and conform.

16. Other omissions. No Rule 14a-5(e)(4) universal-proxy notice deadline for 2026 (about April 13, 2026). Rule 14a-8 (December 29, 2025), advance-notice and proxy-access dates compute correctly. No appraisal-rights statement (checklist G-07). No say-on-pay frequency/next-vote statement (Item 24). Confirm form of proxy has FOR/AGAINST/ABSTAIN for directors.

C. TIER 3 - INCONSISTENCIES AND CHECKLIST ERRORS
- Board meetings: draft 7; checklist D-07 says 8.
- D-13 cites Nasdaq Rule 5606 though Pinnacle is NYSE-listed; no diversity matrix exists; the qualifications matrix is blank.
- Villanueva "director since 2022" vs. "Board member since January 1, 2024"; Harmon CEO "2010-2023" vs. "President and CEO 2012-2020"; Chen's Axton start (2017 in questionnaire; 2019 in proxy).
- Tech Oversight Committee "formed 2023" vs. email's "first year"; confirm.
- Tax fees rose 79% ($290,000 to $520,000); explain pre-approval.
- Checklist summary shows 3 N/A in Director category; only D-11 and D-15 are N/A.
- Pay ratio annualizes new-hire pay; Item 402(u) instruction does not permit annualizing part-time/seasonal employees. Recompute after item 1.
- Mehta: no disclosure of how he was identified (Item 407(c)(2)(vii)); confirm five-year directorships. Proposal 1's contingency on Proposal 4 (majority of outstanding shares) needs clear card instructions.

D. ACTION PLAN
1. April 21-22: resolve items 1-2 with Committee, Rothwell, payroll.
2. Add Broadleaf; fix approval body and independence disclosure.
3. Verify Leland Cross records and 14a-8 timeline.
4. Rebuild PvP (five years, PEO table).
5. Complete Tier 2 fixes; obtain remaining questionnaires (Isaacs, Harmon, Poole, Mehta).
6. Redo the checklist, re-circulate to Committees and Board; move Kensington's April 25 date if necessary.

UNRESOLVED: correct incentive targets/payouts; Leland Cross holding period; Isaacs/Clearway interlock; identity of the 9% holder; unseen questionnaires.
